verdict: Good app, but not top-tier yet
verdict_explanation: Loop 1 fixed the Schema.org honesty leak; loop 2 eliminates the parallel icons array that silently mismatched on content growth. The architecture is flat and increasingly honest. Remaining structural findings are BASE_URL scatter (7 files) and the Hero mockup (cosmetic).

architecture_quality.proof: src/components/BenefitGrid.astro parallel icons array removed this loop; src/content/site.ts:26-39 each benefit now carries its own icon field — TypeScript enforces co-location. Residual: BASE_URL construction still scattered across 7 files (F-003/F2 in backlog).

state_management.proof: src/content/site.ts — as const literal; zero mutable runtime state; static site generator pipeline; no writers, no readers, no persistence seam.

concurrency.proof: No async/await, no Promise, no event handlers, no Task constructs in any source file. Astro SSG builds synchronous template trees at build time. Concurrency is genuinely N/A for a static site generator.

test_strategy.proof: Zero test files in repo. astro check provides type correctness only. No behavioral, semantic, or integration tests. 9-anchor (tests targeting real Interfaces) not met — framework-constrained acceptable residual for a static site with no runtime domain logic.

credibility.proof: Loop 1 commit 56056b6 fixed Schema.org honesty leak (F-001 resolved). Loop 2 eliminates parallel-array invariant violation (F-002 resolved). Both visible honesty hazards gone. Remaining residual: Hero.astro:28-63 hardcoded tile labels disconnected from site.ts — cosmetic severity.

domain_modeling.proof: src/content/site.ts:26-39 — each benefits[] entry now carries an icon field typed as string by as const. Missing icon = TypeScript type error at build time. Domain model for benefits is now complete. Residual: Hero.astro tile labels remain disconnected from site.ts (cosmetic).

data_flow.proof: import { site } from '../content/site' is the single data source; all components import from it. DAG clean — no back-channels. Residual: import.meta.env.BASE_URL transformation repeated at 9 call sites across 7 files with two inconsistent patterns (F-003/F2 still open).

Loop 2: benefit icons now sourced from site.ts via benefit.icon — Fragment set:html={benefit.icon} idiom used correctly, no index-based access. Residual blocking 9.5: BASE_URL construction without a shared url() helper (F-003/F2) — non-idiomatic pattern duplicated across 7 files.

simplicity.proof: BenefitGrid.astro frontmatter reduced from 9 lines (7-line icons const + 2 import lines) to 2 lines (import only); site.ts gains 3 icon fields co-located with benefit data. Net: fewer lines, less ceremony, no index arithmetic. Residual: Hero.astro:28-286 still carries 220 lines of hardcoded mockup (F-003/F3, cosmetic).

findings.title: BenefitGrid parallel icons array silently mismatches on content growth
findings.why_it_matters: Adding a fourth benefit to site.ts produces a silently-broken card with no icon, undetectable until visual QA.
findings.what_is_wrong: BenefitGrid.astro:4-8 defined const icons = [svg1, svg2, svg3] (3 entries). At line 15, site.benefits.map((benefit, i) => ... icons[i]) indexed into this array. If a fourth benefit were added, icons[3] would be undefined and Fragment set:html renders empty — no TypeScript error, no build warning.
findings.leverage_impact: Callers (editors of site.ts) could not know that adding a benefit without also updating BenefitGrid.astro breaks the UI.
findings.locality_impact: A domain content change (site.ts) required a parallel implementation change (BenefitGrid.astro) with no mechanical enforcement.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Silently broken UI on content growth; invariant violation unenforceable by type system.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Move SVG icon strings into each benefit entry in site.ts as an icon field. Template reads benefit.icon directly. TypeScript enforces field presence — missing icon = type error at build time. This loop executed this fix.

findings.title: BASE_URL construction repeated at 9 call sites across 7 files with inconsistent patterns
findings.why_it_matters: Any URL convention change requires touching 7 files with two inconsistent patterns that can produce broken links on GitHub Pages.
findings.what_is_wrong: Two construction patterns: (1) ${BASE_URL}${link.href.replace(/^\//, '')} in SiteHeader.astro:19,33; (2) bare ${BASE_URL}support concatenation in SiteFooter.astro:10-12, FAQList.astro:33, support.astro:71-73. Pattern 2 works only because literals happen not to have leading slashes. Changing SiteFooter's href to '/support' would produce double-slash on GitHub Pages.
findings.leverage_impact: Each call site must independently know the BASE_URL transformation rule including the slash-stripping quirk.
findings.locality_impact: URL convention change requires touching 7 files; inconsistency means some sites are more fragile than others.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Inconsistent URL construction can ship a broken link to production; fragile invariant spread across 7 files.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Extract a url(path: string): string helper in src/utils/url.ts. All 9 call sites become url('support'), url('/'), etc. Deletion test: removing helper forces complexity back to 9 callers — it earns its keep.

findings.title: Hero device mockup is 220 lines of hardcoded simulation disconnected from site.ts
findings.why_it_matters: Tile labels in the hero visual will drift from the real app's content with zero build-time warning.
findings.what_is_wrong: Hero.astro:28-63 contains 12 hardcoded .sb-tile labels and player title 'Game Opener Mix' (Hero.astro:67), all disconnected from site.ts. ~165 CSS lines for the mockup.
findings.leverage_impact: None: the mockup is pure HTML/CSS with no reuse.
findings.locality_impact: Changes to app tile naming require manual hunting in Hero.astro, not site.ts.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Maintenance drift between hero visual and real app is invisible.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Replace the hardcoded device mockup with a real screenshot from site.screenshots[0] framed in the existing .device-frame CSS, or source tile labels from a site.ts heroTiles array. Option (a) is simpler — removes ~50 HTML lines and ~120 CSS lines.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: F1 fix (parallel icons → benefit.icon): passes deletion test — icons const disappears cleanly, complexity collapses into data. No new seam created.
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: BenefitGrid.astro frontmatter reduced from 9 lines to 2 lines. Icon co-location with content eliminates the two-file edit requirement.
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Extracting an icon component, adding a mapping object, or introducing a registry — all add ceremony without reducing ambiguity.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: No tests exist; none needed. Build-time TypeScript (as const) enforces icon field presence. astro check is the verification gate — passes with 0 errors, 0 hints.

backlog.title: Extract url() helper to consolidate BASE_URL construction across 7 files
backlog.why_it_matters: 7-file touch radius for URL convention change; two inconsistent patterns that can produce broken links on GitHub Pages.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Any map(..., i) => sideArray[i] pattern where two arrays are maintained separately.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Co-locate the associated data in the same object. If an icon belongs to a benefit, it is a property of the benefit — icon travels with the data in site.ts.
builder_notes.stack_example: In site.ts: benefits: [{ title: '...', body: '...', icon: '<svg>...</svg>' }] — icon travels with the benefit.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Same env var read + string transform repeated in 7+ files across the codebase.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: One function url(path) that owns the convention. All callers use it. Deletion test: if you delete the function, the problem comes back in all callers — it earns its keep.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: JSON-LD in a layout that contains prices, dates, or feature flags that also appear in a separate content module.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Either derive JSON-LD values from the content module (DRY), or omit claims the code cannot authoritatively make.
builder_notes.stack_example: BaseLayout.astro: derive offer price from site.pricing.free (truthfully free) and omit the pro offer until a numeric price exists.

narrative: Good, not winning yet. Loop 2 lands cleanly: the parallel icons array is gone, benefit domain objects now carry their own visual metadata, and TypeScript enforces the invariant at build time. Remaining structural work is the BASE_URL scatter (7 files, two inconsistent patterns) — one more loop should close it. Test strategy is zero, which is honest for a static site with no runtime domain logic. State management and concurrency are genuinely N/A at 10. The hero mockup is real drift risk but cosmetic for contest. If the BASE_URL helper lands cleanly in loop 3, the site's architecture will be as tight as it can get without adding test infrastructure the site genuinely does not need.

loop_result.what_changed: Moved SVG icon strings from BenefitGrid.astro icons const into site.ts benefits[].icon fields; updated BenefitGrid.astro to use benefit.icon instead of icons[i]; removed the icons const entirely.
loop_result.evidence_change_is_honest: npm run build: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints, 5 pages built. astro check clean. TypeScript enforces icon field presence via as const — missing field is a compile-time error.

implementation_review.reason: All three checks passed; parallel icons array is fully removed from BenefitGrid.astro; site.ts benefits[] now carry icon fields with TypeScript enforcement; no regression introduced.
